  #openapi?: Client<paths> & ((scope: { token: string }) => FixtureClient);
  /**
   * Calls for one recipient, with the recipient token as the only credential.
   *
   * Call it: `fixture.client({ token })` returns the scope. Read it: `fixture.client.GET(…)` is the typed
   * `openapi-fetch` escape hatch over this client's credential and base URL (it does not retry).
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * const inbox = await fixture.client({ token }).inbox.list();
   * ```
   */
  get client(): Client<paths> & ((scope: { token: string }) => FixtureClient) {
    return (this.#openapi ??= Object.assign((scope: { token: string }) => this.#tokenScope(scope), createOpenAPIClient<paths>(this._client)));
  }
  #tokenScope(scope: { token: string }): FixtureClient {
    const token = scope?.token;
    if (typeof token !== "string" || token.trim() === "") throw new ConfigurationError("client({ token }) needs a non-empty token.");
    if (token.startsWith("pcft_")) {
      throw new ConfigurationError("client({ token }) was given a workspace API key. Pass the short-lived token your backend minted; never ship an API key to a browser or an app.");
    }
    // Only the token: no API key, no environment fallback, no workspace (the token names it).
    const { apiKey: _apiKey, auth: _auth, workspaceId: _workspaceId, credentialFromEnv: _env, dangerouslyAllowBrowser: _browser, ...rest } = this.#options;

  /**
   * Calls scoped to one community. Chain `.as(actorId)` to act as a user.
   * @param communityId - `{community_id}`
   */
